newsitem.title: USA: Micron Technology says low prices hurt Q1.
newsitem.headline: Micron Technology says low prices hurt Q1.

text.p: Micron Technology Inc said "significantly lower pricing" for memory chips was the main reason that its first quarter sales and earnings declined sharply from a year ago.
The chip maker said the average selling price per megabit of memory chip fell 84 percent in the first quarter of 1997 just ended when compared with the first quarter of 1996.
Earlier Micron Technology reported net income fell to $0.10 a share on sales of $728.1 million in the first quarter ended Nov 28 from $1.51 a share on sales of $1.185 billion in the year ago quarter.
Prices also fell in the first quarter of 1997 from its 1996 fourth quarter by an average 22 percent per megabit, the company said.

But Micron Technology said its semiconductor operations more than doubled megabit production in the first quarter from the same quarter of 1996 and increased production 48 percent in the three months from the fourth quarter of 1996.
Production increased because it converted its manufacturing operations to 8-inch wafers and made its primary product 16 Meg DRAMs (dynamic random access memory chips) instead of 4 Meg DRAMS.
Micron Technology said its personal computer business saw unit sales grow 22 percent in the first quarter from the same year-earlier quarter.
The gross margin in its PC business improved 75 percent from the previous year, which it attributed mostly to declining costs of components.

Saying it is evaluating financing alternatives after having paid off all its bank lines of credit, Micron Technology said it expects to file a shelf registration statement for up to $1 billion in debt or equity securities to give it flexibility.

Micron's first quarter profit of $0.10 a share included a gain of $0.03 a share for an investment gain. According to First Call, Micron was expected to post a profit of $0.04 a share for the first quarter.
